## The question

[single valued function and multi valued function](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2594410/single-valued-function-and-multi-valued-function), asked by [Rajesh kushwaha](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/488673/rajesh-kushwaha) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-01-06; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> square root function is a multi valued function. for example 16 have two square root 4 and -4. but it is violation of the definition of function that each element of domain has one and only one image. then how it is a function. please clear my dout.
:::

> for example 16 have two square root 4 and -4.

Yes, that is correct.

> square root function is a multi valued function.

Not quite.  Square roots are different from the square root function.  The definition of $\sqrt{x}$ is not *all* numbers $y$ satisfying $y^2=x$, but the unique nonnegative number $y$ such that $y^2=x$.  

Thus $\sqrt{16} = 4$, not $4$ and $-4$.  

With this restriction, $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ is a function with domain $[0,\infty)$.
